name: Aadavan
etymology: Established modern Tamil given name; Tamil ādavan 'sun' (not a Sanskrit dictionary headword)

name: Aadhya
etymology: Fem. of ādya

name: Aahna
etymology: Established modern Hindu given name; modern coinage, sometimes linked to Skt ahan 'day' — no attestation of this exact form

name: Aanya
meaning: A contemporary Indian name; exact origin uncertain.
etymology: A modern Indian name in wide use. Its exact derivation is not settled, so no single classical meaning is claimed.

name: Aaradhya
meaning: Worthy of worship; to be worshipped
etymology: Worthy of worship; one who is to be worshipped; epithet associated with Lakṣmī and Rādhā.

name: Aarav
etymology: Ārava — 'a cry, sound, noise, roar'. MW: 'sound, noise, cry.' Popular modern usage; resonates with music, voice, expression.

name: Aarna
etymology: Wave, flood, stream; the feminine form arṇā lemmatized as 'river' in MW.

name: Aarush
etymology: Āruṣa — 'reddish, ruddy; the rising sun'. MW: 'red, reddish; the sun.' Vedic adjective evoking dawn's colour. Popular modern usage.

name: Aarushi
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. aruṣa/aruṣī: 'red, ruddy; red mare; dawn' (RV)

name: Aarya
etymology: MW āryā f.:

name: Aayush
etymology: Modern shortened form of MW-attested āyuṣmant. Standalone Āyush as a personal name is 20th-century usage.

name: Abhay
etymology: Without fear; the state granted by the divine to devotees; the abhaya-mudra is the gesture of fearlessness.

name: Abhijeet
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. abhijit: 'victorious, one who conquers'; also name of a nakshatra/star

name: Abhinandan
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. abhinandana: 'rejoicing, delighting in; greeting, welcome'

name: Abhinav
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. abhinava: 'quite new or young, fresh'

name: Abhinay
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. abhinaya: 'indication of a sentiment by gesture, dramatic action'

name: Abhishek
etymology: MW abhiṣeka:

name: Adhira
etymology: Modern coinage; marketed as 'lightning' but the MW adjective adhira means 'unsteady' and isn't classically used as a name. DISCLAIMER (2026-08-07 policy): the Sanskrit lookalike adhīra (MW:

name: Aditi
etymology: Boundless, unbroken, unimpaired; the most ancient of the Indian goddesses, mother of the Ādityas.

name: Aditya
etymology: Āditya — 'descendant of Aditi'; one of the twelve solar deities; epithet of Viṣṇu and the Sun. BG 10.21 'ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ'.

name: Advait
etymology: Non-dual; the central insight of Advaita Vedanta — that ultimate reality is one without a second.

name: Advik
etymology: Modern coinage on the sense of advitīya

name: Ahalya
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ahalyā: 'name of the wife of the sage Gautama'; her story in Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa

name: Ahana
etymology: Dawn; the first ray of light; from ahan (day). Personification per Sāyaṇa's Ṛg Veda commentary.

name: Ajay
etymology: The unconquered one; victory that cannot be reversed. Used as an epithet of Vishnu and many heroes in epic literature.

name: Ajit
etymology: Invincible, never defeated; a name of Vishnu, particularly in his role as preserver who cannot be overcome by adharma.

name: Akash
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ākāśa: 'free or open space, sky, ether'

name: Akhil
etymology: Whole, complete, entire; without any part missing.

name: Akriti
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ākṛti: 'form, figure, shape, appearance'

name: Akshara
etymology: Imperishable; syllable; letter; in Vedānta, the unchanging absolute.

name: Akshat
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. akṣata: 'not crushed, uninjured, whole; unhusked grains (for worship)'

name: Akshay
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. akṣaya: 'exempt from decay, undecaying, imperishable'

name: Amal
etymology: Pure, free from stain or defect; ritually clean.

name: Amala
etymology: Spotless, stainless, pure; epithet of the goddess Lakṣmī.

name: Aman
etymology: Arabic amān, via Hindi-Urdu/Punjabi:

name: Amar
etymology: Immortal, deathless; belonging to the realm of the devas. The dictionary Amarakosha takes its name from this quality.

name: Amaya
etymology: MW a-māya:

name: Amit
etymology: Boundless, immeasurable; one whose qualities cannot be limited or counted.

name: Amita
etymology: Boundless, immeasurable, infinite (feminine of Amita).

name: Amoli
etymology: Established modern given name; Hindi amol/amoli 'priceless', from Skt amūlya 'invaluable'

name: Amrutha
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. amṛta: 'immortal; nectar, ambrosia, the drink of immortality'

name: Anaisha
etymology: modern given name; no MW/Apte attestation of this form (possibly an-aiśa or a phonetic coinage)

name: Anamika
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. anāmikā: 'the ring-finger' (lit. 'the nameless one')

name: Anand
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ānanda: 'happiness, joy, enjoyment, pleasure; pure bliss'

name: Anant
etymology: Endless, infinite; the cosmic serpent Shesha on whom Vishnu reclines, representing eternity.

name: Ananya
etymology: Unique; without another; matchless; identical with the divine.

name: Anasuya
meaning: Free of envy; wife of sage Atri
etymology: Freedom from envy or spite; wife of sage Atri in the Rāmāyaṇa, who teaches Sītā wifely dharma.

name: Anaya
etymology: Arabic (variant of Inaya): ’ināya

name: Anika
etymology: Front, face, splendour; the front-rank of an army; the modern soft gloss is 'grace.'

name: Aniket
meaning: One without a home; epithet of Śiva
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. aniketa: 'houseless, homeless, having no fixed abode'; cf. Bhagavad Gita 12.19 'aniketaḥ'

name: Anil
meaning: Wind, breath; one of the eight Vasus
etymology: Wind, breath, air; one of the eight Vasus presiding over natural elements.

name: Anish
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. anīśa: 'having no lord or superior, supreme'; also 'not master of oneself, dependent'

name: Anisha
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. aniśa/aniśam: 'continual, uninterrupted; without night'

name: Anita
etymology: Spanish/European: diminutive of Ana (Anne), ultimately Hebrew Hannah

name: Anjali
etymology: The gesture of cupped hands held together; a posture of reverence, salutation, and benediction; widely used in stotra literature.

name: Ankit
etymology: MW aṅkita:

name: Ankur
etymology: Sprout, new shoot, the first emergence of a seed; the beginning of growth.

name: Anmol
etymology: modern given name; Hindi anmol 'priceless'; root Skt mūlya 'value'

name: Ansh
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. aṃśa: 'a share, portion, part, party; a division'

name: Anushka
etymology: modern given name; commonly treated as a diminutive (also a Slavic diminutive of Anna); no MW/Apte attestation of anuṣkā

name: Anvi
etymology: Modern coinage gaining traction in 2010s-2020s urban India. Marketed as a short feminine form but has no standalone MW lemma.

name: Aparna
meaning: Leafless; epithet of Pārvatī after austerities
etymology: 'Not having even leaves for food during her austerities'; epithet of Pārvatī after her extreme penance to win Śiva.

name: Aradhana
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ārādhana: 'propitiation, worship, adoration; accomplishment, gratifying'

name: Aravind
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. aravinda: 'a lotus (Nelumbium Speciosum); a blue lotus'

name: Aria
etymology: Modern Italian-origin name 'Aria' (musical 'melody'); adopted into Indian usage 2015+. No MW lemma. Phonetically resonates with Sanskrit ārya 'noble' though etymologically unrelated.

name: Arjun
etymology: Bright, silvery-white; the third Pandava prince, recipient of the Bhagavad Gita.

name: Arnav
etymology: MW arṇava:

name: Arun
etymology: The reddish glow of dawn; the charioteer of Surya (the sun), brother of Garuda, son of Kashyapa and Vinata.

name: Aryan
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ārya: 'noble, honourable, respectable; an Aryan'; the -n form is a modern rendering

name: Asha
etymology: Hope, desire, expectation, prospect; one of the personified concepts in early Sanskrit literature.

name: Ashwin
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. aśvin: 'possessed of horses; the two Aśvins (divine twin horsemen)'; also month Āśvina

name: Atharva
etymology: The fourth Veda; an ancient sage; in some traditions, a son of Ganesha.

name: Atul
etymology: Incomparable, beyond measure or balance; without equal.

name: Avani
etymology: The earth; that which protects; also river, stream, course.

name: Avi
etymology: modern given name, commonly a short form of Avinash/Abhinav; MW s.v. avi = 'sheep, ram; mountain' (not the intended sense)

name: Avinash
etymology: Indestructible; that which cannot be destroyed; the -in stem gives the adjectival/agentive sense.

name: Avya
etymology: Modern coinage popular in 2020s. Marketed with various meanings but no MW lemma as standalone feminine name.

name: Ayaan
etymology: Modern name; Skt ayana =

name: Ayansh
etymology: Modern Sanskritic-flavored coinage in the -ansh family (Reyansh, Priyansh). No MW lemma; built from Hindi/Sanskrit phonetics.

name: Bhagwant
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. bhagavat/bhagavant: 'fortunate, blessed, holy, divine; the Lord'

name: Bhargav
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. bhārgava: 'descendant of Bhṛgu' (e.g. Śukra, Paraśurāma)

name: Bhaskar
etymology: Resplendent; the sun; fire; a hero. Widely attested epithet of Sūrya.

name: Bhaumik
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. bhaumika: 'relating to the earth, terrestrial; a landholder'

name: Bhavika
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. bhāvika: 'actually being; natural; full of feeling, expressive of emotion'

name: Bhavin
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. bhāvin: 'becoming, being, existing; about to be, future'

name: Bhavna
etymology: Reflection, contemplation; mental cultivation, meditation; in Mīmāṃsā the productive activity.

name: Bhavya
etymology: Modern usage of MW adjective bhavya (splendid). Feminine personal name is a 20th-century usage, not classically attested as a given name.

name: Bhim
etymology: Second Pāṇḍava prince, son of Kunti and Vāyu; renowned for superhuman strength and valor. BG 1.4 'bhīmārjuna-samā'.

name: Bhima
etymology: Feminine of Bhīma; epithet of Devī in awe-inspiring aspect; also a sacred river of the Deccan.

name: Bhimsen
etymology: Full epithet of Bhīma the Pāṇḍava — 'one who possesses a formidable army'. BG 1.10 'balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam'.

name: Bhishma
etymology: Devavrata's vow-name; one who undertook the fearsome celibacy vow. Grandsire of the Kuru lineage. BG 1.8.

name: Bhumi
etymology: The earth, soil, ground; earth-goddess (Pṛthivī); foster-mother of Sītā; consort/form of Lakṣmī.

name: Bhushan
etymology: Ornament, decoration; one of 36 lakṣaṇa of dramatic composition.

name: Bodhi
etymology: Bodhi (बोधि) means perfect knowledge by which one becomes a buddha; supreme enlightenment. MW lists as both M and F. Pan-Indic resonance (Bodhi tree, Bodhini Ekadashi).

name: Chahat
etymology: Hindi-Urdu word for 'desire/love.' Used as a feminine name in modern North Indian families; no Sanskrit root.

name: Chandan
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. candana: 'sandal (tree, wood, or the unctuous preparation of it)'

name: Chandra
etymology: The moon; one of the Navagraha; shining, glittering.

name: Charu
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. cāru: 'agreeable, approved, esteemed; pleasing, lovely, beautiful'

name: Charulata
etymology: Beautiful creeper; transparent compound. Tagore-era literary coinage (Bengali novella character) but both roots MW-attested.

name: Charvi
etymology: beautiful

name: Chetan
etymology: MW:

name: Chetana
etymology: Consciousness; intelligence; awareness; opposed to acetana (insentience).

name: Chetna
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. cetanā: 'consciousness, understanding, sense, intelligence'

name: Chinmay
etymology: Consisting of pure consciousness; spiritual; the Universal Self.

name: Chirag
etymology: From Persian چراغ (cherāgh)

name: Chudala
etymology: Saintly queen of Śikhidhvaja in the Yoga-vāsiṣṭha. Attained Self-knowledge before her husband and led him to brahma-jñāna through the Cūḍālā-Śikhidhvaja-saṃvāda.

name: Chudamani
etymology: Cūḍāmaṇi — 'jewel worn on the top of the head, crest-jewel'; figuratively 'the best, most excellent.' Sītā's divine crown-jewel given to Hanumān in Aśokavana as token for Rāma.

name: Daaman
etymology: MW: dāman n. 'string, thread, fillet, rope; chaplet, garland; gift'. Element in Dāmodara and Indra-dāman (Yādava).

name: Daanta
etymology: MW: dāntā occurs as a proper name. Purāṇa: 'Dāntā is an apsaras of Alakāpurī who danced in honour of Aṣṭāvakra.'

name: Daivik
etymology: Modern Sanskritic usage of MW adjective daivika (divine). Personal-name usage is 21st-century.

name: Daksh
etymology: Able, fit, expert, clever; one of Brahmā's mind-born sons; Prajāpati identified with the Aditya.

name: Damayanti
etymology: Daughter of King Bhīma of Vidarbha; wife of Nala; central heroine of the Nalopākhyāna in the Mahābhārata Vana-parva.

name: Damodara
meaning: Kṛṣṇa; bound at the belly with a rope
etymology: Epithet of Kṛṣṇa commemorating Yaśodā binding the child Kṛṣṇa to a mortar; listed as the 367th name in the Viṣṇu-sahasranāma. MW: 'N. of Krishna' from dāman + udara.

name: Darshan
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. darśana: 'seeing, observing, sight; audience; view, doctrine'

name: Daruka
etymology: Dāruka, the loyal sārathi of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, appears repeatedly in the Mahābhārata (Udyoga, Drona, Mauṣala Parvans). MW: 'N. of Krishna's charioteer'.

name: Deepak
etymology: MW dīpaka:

name: Deepal
etymology: modern given name; root Skt dīpa 'lamp, light'; no classical headword for dīpal

name: Deepika
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. dīpikā: 'a light, lamp, lantern; that which illustrates'

name: Dev
etymology: MW deva:

name: Devaki
meaning: Daughter of Devaka; mother of Kṛṣṇa
etymology: Mother of Kṛṣṇa; wife of Vasudeva; identified with Aditi and Dākṣāyaṇī in Purāṇic theology.

name: Deval
etymology: Devala — Vedic seer of Kāśyapa-Śāṇḍilya gotra, disciple of Vyāsa. Named in BG 10.13.

name: Devan
etymology: modern given name (Tamil Tēvan, 'king/god'); MW s.v. devana = 'gambling, dice-play' (a different, unintended sense)

name: Devansh
etymology: MW devāṃśa:

name: Devanshi
etymology: modern Sanskritic given name; roots Skt deva + aṃśa; not a classical headword

name: Devarshi
etymology: Devarṣi — 'sage among the gods, celestial ṛṣi', principally Nārada. BG 10.13 names him explicitly.

name: Devasena
meaning: Army of the gods; Skanda's wife
etymology: Devasenā — 'army of the gods, personified'. Daughter of Prajāpati; given by Brahmā as wife to Skanda — hence Skanda = Devasenāpati.

name: Devavrat
etymology: Devavrata — 'one whose vow is divine'. Birth-name of Bhīṣma, son of Śāntanu and Gaṅgā; named Bhīṣma only after his terrible vow.

name: Devdas
etymology: Devadāsa — 'servant or attendant of God / a temple-servant'. Used as personal name across India.

name: Devdatt
etymology: God-given; the name of Arjuna's conch shell in the Bhagavad-gītā; also a vital air.

name: Devendra
etymology: Devendra — 'chief/lord of the gods', standard epithet of Indra. Compound deva-indra resolves by guṇa.

name: Devesh
etymology: Deveśa — 'lord of the gods', epithet of Śiva (Śivapurāṇa 2.1.13), of Kṛṣṇa, and of the supreme deity in Śākta literature.

name: Devika
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. devikā: 'a minor goddess'; also name of a river

name: Devnath
etymology: Devanātha — 'lord of the gods', epithet of Śiva. Also one of the Nine Nāthas in the Gorakhanātha tradition.

name: Devraj
etymology: Devarāja — 'king of the gods', Vedic and Purāṇic epithet of Indra as sovereign of Svarga.

name: Devyani
etymology: Devayānī — daughter of Śukrācārya (preceptor of Asuras); fell in love with Kaca, then married King Yayāti. Mother of Yadu and Turvasu.

name: Dhairya
etymology: MW noun dhairya (patience) used as a modern masculine given name; not classically attested as a personal name.

name: Dhanush
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. dhanus: 'a bow; the sign Sagittarius; a measure of length'

name: Dhanya
etymology: Bestowing wealth; blessed, lucky, happy; also Emblic myrobalan.

name: Dhaval
etymology: MW: white, dazzling white; also handsome, beautiful; pure. A widely used given name today, especially in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

name: Dhruv
etymology: Fixed, eternal; the polar star; the boy-prince devotee of Viṣṇu per BhP 4.8-12.

name: Dhruva
etymology: Polar-star personified; nakṣatra class 'fixed' (Uttara Phālgunī etc.).

name: Diksha
etymology: Consecration; initiation for a sacrifice or into a mantra/sect; ritual purification.

name: Dilip
etymology: King of the Ikṣvāku/Solar race; son of Aṃśumān and father of Bhagīratha; great Raghu-vaṃśa ancestor.

name: Dinesh
meaning: Lord of the day; the sun
etymology: MW:

name: Dipti
etymology: Brightness, light, splendour, beauty; brilliance of beauty; extreme loveliness.

name: Divakar
etymology: Day-maker, the sun; epithet of Sūrya; one of the Ādityas.

name: Divya
etymology: MW:

name: Divyansh
etymology: Modern -ansh family coinage. Components divya + ansh exist in MW but compound as name is 21st-century.

name: Divyanshu
etymology: modern Sanskritic given name; roots Skt divya + aṃśu (MW s.v. aṃśu 'ray, sunbeam'); compound not a classical headword

name: Diya
etymology: Hindi/Urdu word for oil lamp (from Persian dīyā). Hugely popular feminine name post-2000s. No Sanskrit lemma.

name: Drishti
etymology: MW noun dṛṣṭi (sight) used as a modern feminine name. Personal-name usage is 20th-century.

name: Durg
etymology: Literally 'difficult of access' — a fortress; also an epithet of Śiva.

name: Durga
etymology: The supreme Devī, slayer of Mahiṣāsura; principal form of Pārvatī. MW: 'invincible'.

name: Durgesh
etymology: Wisdomlib (Purāṇa):

name: Dushyant
meaning: King of Lunar dynasty; husband of Śakuntalā
etymology: Reputed King of the Lunar dynasty (MW); husband of Śakuntalā and father of Bharata, eponymous ancestor of the Bhārata lineage.

name: Ekansh
etymology: Modern -ansh family coinage from eka + ansh. Compound as personal name is 21st-century.

name: Esha
meaning: Modern form of isha (fem. of Isha)
etymology: MW lemma īśā exists (feminine of Īśa) but standalone use as a personal name is modern North Indian convention; pronounced 'Esha.'

name: Eva
etymology: Hebrew/European name (Eve/Eva) adopted by diaspora and urban Indian families for its short phonetic and pan-cultural feel. No Sanskrit root.

name: Gagandeep
etymology: MW: gagana 'sky'; dīpa 'lamp' (compound modern)

name: Ganesh
meaning: Lord of Śiva's gaṇas; elephant-headed god
etymology: Son of Śiva and Pārvatī; elephant-headed deity of beginnings and remover of obstacles; scribe of the Mahābhārata at Vyāsa's request.

name: Ganga
etymology: Sacred river-goddess; descended to earth through Bhagīratha's penance to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons.

name: Gargi
etymology: MW:

name: Garima
etymology: Heaviness, dignity; in classical yoga the siddhi of becoming infinitely heavy.

name: Gaurav
etymology: MW: gaurava 'weight, importance, respect, dignity'

name: Gauri
etymology: Brilliant goddess; Śiva's wife Pārvatī (the fair-complexioned).

name: Gautam
etymology: MW: gautama, patronymic; name of the Buddha

name: Gayatri
etymology: The Gāyatrī metre (24 syllables); the mantra-goddess personifying Ṛg Veda 3.62.10 — one of the most sacred Vedic verses.

name: Girish
etymology: MW:

name: Gita
etymology: 'The sung one'; song; the namesake of the Bhagavad-Gītā itself, the sacred song of Kṛṣṇa.

name: Gopal
etymology: A king; a cowherd; Kṛṣṇa as protector of cows.

name: Govind
etymology: Kṛṣṇa as protector and finder of cows; one of the most-invoked Kṛṣṇa epithets.

name: Hanuman
etymology: Son of Vāyu and Añjanā; chief of Rāma's vānara army; leapt to Laṅkā to find Sītā.

name: Hardik
etymology: MW: hārdika 'hearty, cordial, from the heart'

name: Hari
etymology: One who takes away (sins/sorrows); pervasive epithet of Viṣṇu and Kṛṣṇa; also signifies the colour yellow-green.

name: Harleen
etymology: Punjabi (Sikh formation): Har (God, standard Gurbani name) + leen (absorbed, engrossed — from Sanskrit līna) =

name: Harsha
etymology: Apte harṣa (Apte's own sense order):

name: Harshit
etymology: MW harṣita:

name: Hazel
etymology: English botanical name adopted by NRI diaspora families. No Sanskrit root; included for diaspora coverage.

name: Hem
etymology: Gold; horse of dark colour. Widely lexicographer-attested.

name: Hema
etymology: A celestial courtesan; Apsaras of Indra's court; in Hari-vaṃśa among the Apsaras list.

name: Hemant
etymology: Early winter; one of the six ṛtus; associated with certain austerities.

name: Hetvi
etymology: reason, cause

name: Himanshu
etymology: 'Cool-rayed', the moon; also camphor. Pervasive in kāvya including Meghadūta 91, Raghuvaṃśa 5.16.

name: Hita
etymology: MW:

name: Hiya
etymology: Hindi/Bengali word for 'heart' (from prākṛt hiyā). Popular feminine name in 2010s-2020s. No Sanskrit lemma as personal name.

name: Hutashan
etymology: Hutāśana — 'oblation-eater'; classical Vedic epithet of Agni, the fire-god, as the deity who consumes the burnt offerings of the yajña. Most common kāvya-name for fire.

name: Ila
meaning: Earth; speech; offering; daughter of Manu
etymology: The earth; flow of praise/speech personified as a goddess; daughter of Manu and mother of Purūravas.

name: Inaya
etymology: Arabic/Urdu word ’ināya (care) used as feminine name in Muslim and increasingly Hindu urban families. No Sanskrit root.

name: Indira
etymology: Epithet of Lakṣmī (consort of Viṣṇu); also 'beauty, splendour.'

name: Indivar
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. indīvara, n. 'blue lotus (Nymphaea)'

name: Indra
etymology: King of the devas; lord of the heavens; wielder of the vajra; the most-invoked deity of the Ṛg-veda.

name: Indraneel
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. indra-nīla, m. 'a sapphire'

name: Indu
etymology: The moon; a bright drop, especially of Soma; the spark in the sky.

name: Ira
etymology: Irā — 'any drinkable fluid; food, refreshment; the earth; speech'. MW: 'irā, drink, food; the earth; speech.' Vedic feminine; daughter of Dakṣa per Mbh.

name: Isha
etymology: Lord, ruler, master, owner; an epithet of Śiva and Viṣṇu; the opening word of the Īśa Upaniṣad.

name: Ishaan
etymology: Ruler, sovereign; an epithet of Śiva-Rudra; also the regent of the northeastern direction (Īśāna-koṇa).

name: Ishika
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. iṣīkā, f. 'a reed; a painter's brush'

name: Ishita
etymology: Superiority, supremacy, absolute authority; one of the eight Siddhis (yogic attainments) of Śiva.

name: Jagannath
etymology: Lord of the universe; form of Kṛṣṇa worshipped at Purī; principal deity of the Jagannātha cult.

name: Jagriti
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. jāgṛti, f. 'waking, watchfulness, vigilance'

name: Jagruti
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. jāgṛti, f. 'waking, watchfulness, vigilance'

name: Jai
etymology: Conquest, victory; epithet of Viṣṇu and many heroes; one of the two gatekeepers of Vaikuṇṭha (with Vijaya).

name: Jatin
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. jaṭin, 'wearing twisted locks (of Śiva; an ascetic)'

name: Jeevan
etymology: Life, manner of living; that which gives life. Vedic attestation RV 1.48.10.

name: Jharna
etymology: Hindi/Bengali jharnā, from Skt √jhar

name: Jishnu
etymology: Victorious, triumphant; epithet of Arjuna, Viṣṇu, Indra and the Sun. MW: 'victorious, triumphant, winning [RV; AV; VS]; Viṣṇu, Indra, Arjuna.'

name: Jiya
etymology: Hindi word from jīv (life). Popular feminine name in 2000s Bollywood-era urban families. No Sanskrit standalone lemma.

name: Jyoti
etymology: MW jyotis n.:

name: Kabir
meaning: The Great (Arabic kabir); the bhakti poet
etymology: Arabic word kabīr (great); also name of the 15th-century bhakti poet Kabīr. Modern given name has no Sanskrit lemma.

name: Kaira
etymology: Modern Indian/diasporic feminine coinage; no Monier-Williams lemma. Parental association with 'unique, peerless.' Phonetic resonance with Arabic khayra 'good' and Sanskrit-style -ā ending. Popular in 2010s-2020s urban Indian naming.

name: Kairav
etymology: MW s.v. kairava — 'the white esculent water-lily (blossoming at night)'

name: Kajal
etymology: Hindi kājal, from Sanskrit kajjala via Prakrit — MW kajjala:

name: Kalpana
etymology: Imagination, fancy, conception; formation, creation, arrangement; in Āyurveda the preparation/formulation of medicines.

name: Kalyani
etymology: MW s.v. kalyani — 'auspicious, beautiful, illustrious; a cow'

name: Kamakshi
etymology: 'She of love-filled eyes'; an epithet of the Goddess (Devī/Pārvatī); the principal deity of the Kāñcīpuram Kāmākṣī Amman temple.

name: Kamala
etymology: 'The lotus-one'; an epithet of Lakṣmī (consort of Viṣṇu); also signifies an excellent woman.

name: Kanika
etymology: MW s.v. kanika — 'a grain, small particle, atom'

name: Kanishk
etymology: Historical: King Kaniska, Kushan dynasty (epigraphic; Rajatarangini I)

name: Kapil
meaning: Tawny-coloured; sage Kapila; an avatāra of Viṣṇu
etymology: 'Reddish-brown, tawny'; the sage Kapila, traditional founder of the Sāṃkhya system; in Bhāgavata tradition the fifth avatāra of Viṣṇu.

name: Karan
etymology: MW s.v. karna — 'the ear; N. of a celebrated hero of the Mahabharata'

name: Karthik
etymology: Variant short-form spelling for the war-god Kārtikeya; widely used in South Indian Tamil/Telugu form 'Karthik'.

name: Kartikeya
etymology: Son of the Kṛttikā stars (the Pleiades who nursed him); the war-god, commander of the deva army; also known as Skanda, Murugan, Subrahmaṇya.

name: Karun
etymology: Compassion, kindness; in Nāṭyaśāstra one of the eight rasas (the pathetic sentiment); central virtue in both Hindu and Buddhist ethics.

name: Kashyap
etymology: Patronymic from Kaśyapa — the ancient Vedic sage, husband of Aditi and father of the Ādityas; one of the seven primordial ṛṣis (Saptarṣi).

name: Kavita
etymology: Poetry, the art of poetry; a poem; also a classification of Prabandha music per Śārṅgadeva (Saṅgīta-ratnākara).

name: Kavya
etymology: Poetic; pertaining to a kavi/poet; in Sanskrit literary theory the noun kāvya = the body of poetic literature (mahākāvya, dramatic kāvya, etc.).

name: Keshav
etymology: Having long or handsome hair; slayer of Keśin demon; pervasive Vaiṣṇava epithet of Kṛṣṇa.

name: Khem
etymology: Pali/Prakrit form of Sanskrit Kṣema. Pali Khema = 'safe; calm; Nibbāna' (PTS Dict). Borne by King Khema (Bodhisattva in Kakusandha Buddha's time), Khemā Therī (chief female disciple of Buddha in wisdom).

name: Khushboo
etymology: Persian khuš-bū

name: Khushi
etymology: Persian/Urdu word khushī (happiness) used as feminine name; ubiquitous in 2000s North Indian families. No Sanskrit root.

name: Kia
etymology: Modern hypocoristic likely influenced by Korean/Western names and Kaira-family Indian coinages. No Sanskrit root.

name: Kiaan
etymology: Modern coinage marketed with Persian (kiyān = king) and Sanskrit overtones. No MW lemma; popular post-2010 in urban India and NRI families.

name: Kiara
etymology: Modern Italian/Latin-origin name 'Kiara' (from chiara 'clear, bright'), adopted into Indian usage as Sanskrit-flavored feminine in 2010s. No MW lemma. Some parents associate with Sanskrit kiyā 'how much' — not etymologically sound.

name: Kinnar
etymology: Kinnara — 'what kind of man?'; class of celestial musicians, half-human half-horse (or half-bird), who attend Kubera. Devoted to music.

name: Kiran
etymology: Kiraṇa — 'a ray of light, beam, sunbeam'. Very popular modern Indian given name.

name: Kirana
etymology: Kiraṇā — feminine of kiraṇa. Both spellings used as personal name.

name: Kiritin
etymology: Kirīṭin — 'one wearing the diadem'; epithet of Arjuna in BG 11.17 and 11.46, also a vibhūti-name of Viṣṇu.

name: Kirti
etymology: Kīrti — 'fame, glory, renown'. BG 10.34: among the divine feminine qualities Kṛṣṇa lists. Also a Dakṣa-daughter in Purāṇic genealogies.

name: Kirtiman
etymology: Kīrtimān — 'possessing fame'. Eldest son of Vasudeva and Devakī, killed at birth by Kaṃsa (Bhāgavata 10.1).

name: Kishor
etymology: Kiśora — 'a youth, an adolescent boy'. Used especially of the young Kṛṣṇa in Vraja-līlā contexts (kiśora-Kṛṣṇa).

name: Kishori
etymology: Kiśorī — 'a young girl'. Used especially of young Rādhā (Kiśorī-Rādhā) in Vaiṣṇava devotional contexts.

name: Komal
etymology: Tender, delicate, soft; gentle, charming, sweet.

name: Komala
etymology: Feminine of komala; epithet of Lakṣmī's gentle aspect.

name: Koyal
etymology: MW s.v. kokila — 'the (black or Indian) cuckoo'

name: Krish
etymology: Modern 20th-century shortening of Kṛṣṇa, popularized by Bollywood and NRI families seeking a short portable form. Standalone form not MW-attested.

name: Krishna
etymology: 'The dark one'; the eighth avatāra of Viṣṇu; speaker of the Bhagavad-gītā. Pervasive in epic and Purāṇic literature.

name: Kuber
meaning: Lord of wealth; regent of the north
etymology: God of wealth, treasurer of the gods, dikpāla guarding the northern quarter.

name: Kulish
etymology: Thunderbolt weapon of Indra, synonymous with vajra; signifies irresistible power.

name: Kumar
etymology: Sanskrit kumāra means youth, boy, prince, or son; famously the epithet of Skanda-Kārtikeya, the youthful war-god and son of Śiva.

name: Kumari
etymology: Kumārī means an unmarried young girl or virgin; epithet of Durgā in the kumārī-pūjā rite.

name: Kumud
etymology: White water-lily that blooms by moonlight, symbolising purity and beauty.

name: Kunal
etymology: Aśoka's son, named for the kuṇāla bird (a kind of cuckoo) whose eyes his resembled.

name: Kundal
etymology: Ring-shaped earring; Karṇa was born with divine kuṇḍalas and armour.

name: Kunti
etymology: Also called Pṛthā; wife of Pāṇḍu and mother of Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, and Karṇa.

name: Kuru
meaning: Eponymous ancestor of the Kuru dynasty
etymology: Purāṇic king, son of Saṃvaraṇa, founded the Kuru dynasty central to Mahābhārata; Kurukṣetra bears his name.

name: Kush
etymology: Sacred darbha grass used in rituals; elder son of Rāma and Sītā, twin of Lava.

name: Kushal
etymology: That which is auspicious, proper, prosperous; also skilled, expert, or in good health.

name: Kusum
etymology: General Sanskrit word for a flower or blossom; symbolises beauty and tenderness.

name: Lakshman
etymology: MW s.v. laksmana — 'having lucky marks; N. of a brother of Rama'

name: Lakshya
etymology: MW noun lakṣya (target) used as masculine personal name in modern era. Not classically attested as given name.

name: Lokesh
etymology: Lord of the world; name of Brahmā; of a Buddha.

name: Luv
etymology: MW s.v. lava — 'a small portion, a little; N. of one of the twin sons of Rama'

name: Madhav
etymology: Epithet of Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu; traditionally glossed as 'consort of Mā (Lakṣmī)' or 'born of Madhu clan'; also the spring season.

name: Madhavi
etymology: Fem. of mādhava; the spring-flower (Hiptage benghalensis); name of Yayāti's daughter in the Gālava episode of Mahābhārata Udyoga-parva.

name: Madhu
etymology: MW s.v. madhu — 'honey, sweet, sweetness; spring'

name: Madhuri
etymology: Sweetness, amiableness, charm, grace; in kāvya theory the rasa-quality mādhurya personified as feminine abstract.

name: Mahalakshmi
etymology: MW s.v. mahalaksmi — 'the great Lakshmi, Sakti of Narayana'

name: Mahesh
etymology: MW s.v. mahesa — 'a great lord; N. of Siva'

name: Mahi
etymology: MW s.v. mahi — 'the earth; a cow; land, ground'

name: Mahira
etymology: Arabic/Persian word māhira (skilled). Popular in Muslim and increasingly Hindu families post-2010s. No Sanskrit root.

name: Mala
etymology: Garland of flowers; necklace; rosary used in japa; in alaṅkāra-śāstra 'mālā' is one of the 36 marks of perfect poetic composition.

name: Malini
etymology: One who wears or makes garlands; in Trika tantra the goddess Mālinī personifies the rearranged Sanskrit alphabet (na to pha); also an epithet of Durgā.

name: Mallika
etymology: MW s.v. mallika — 'Arabian jasmine, Jasminum Zambac'

name: Manasi
etymology: Fem. of mānasa 'mental'; one of the mānasa-kanyās (mind-born daughters); Śivapurāṇa 2.3.44.

name: Manav
etymology: Belonging to or descended from Manu; a human being; in plural the tribes of men.

name: Mandira
etymology: MW s.v. mandira — 'a dwelling, house, habitation, temple'

name: Manisha
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. manīṣā (thought, wisdom, intelligence)

name: Manoj
etymology: MW mano-ja:

name: Mansi
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. mānasa (mānasī f., mental, spiritual)

name: Manya
etymology: To be honored, respected, revered; worthy of homage and reverence (gerundive of √man).

name: Manyata
etymology: Honorableness, worthiness of respect; recognition, acceptance, validity; the abstract noun formed from mānya.

name: Maya
etymology: The cosmic illusion personified; the divine śakti by which the One appears as many; also magic, art, supernatural power; name of Buddha's mother.

name: Medhaja
meaning: Born of sacrifice; epithet of Viṣṇu
etymology: Medhaja literally means 'sprung from sacrifice/wisdom' and appears as a name of Viṣṇu in the Mahābhārata.

name: Meena
meaning: Wife of Himavat; mother of Pārvatī
etymology: Menā is the queen of King Himavat and mother of Pārvatī (Umā) and Gaṅgā, according to the Śivapurāṇa and Rāmāyaṇa.

name: Meenakshi
etymology: 'Fish-eyed'; the principal goddess of the Madurai Mīnākṣī Amman temple; daughter of Kubera per Purāṇa.

name: Menaka
etymology: Menakā is one of the foremost apsarās of Indra's court; sent to disrupt the tapas of Viśvāmitra, she became the mother of Śakuntalā.

name: Mihir
etymology: The sun; epithet attested in Mbh + Kāvya; also a cloud, the wind, the moon, a sage. Famous as Varāhamihira.

name: Mihira
etymology: Modern feminine of mihira (MW: the sun). Feminine personal-name usage is 21st-century.

name: Mira
etymology: Mīrā — name of the 16th-century Rajput princess-saint and Kṛṣṇa-bhakta whose songs (padas) are a cornerstone of bhakti literature. Post-classical: no Vedic/MW lemma but historically attested through her hagiography.

name: Mishti
etymology: Bengali word for 'sweet' used as endearment-turned-name in 2010s urban Bengali and pan-Indian families. No Sanskrit standalone lemma as name.

name: Mohan
etymology: Depriving of consciousness, bewildering, confusing, perplexing, infatuating; epithet of Kṛṣṇa; one of Kāmadeva's arrows.

name: Mohana
etymology: Feminine of Mohana; bewildering, fascinating woman.

name: Mohit
etymology: Stupefied, bewildered, infatuated, deluded; past participle of √muh.

name: Moksh
etymology: Liberation; release from the bondage of mundane life; one of the four puruṣārthas.

name: Murari
etymology: 'Enemy of Mura'; an epithet of Kṛṣṇa/Viṣṇu after slaying the demon Mura.

name: Myra
etymology: Modern English/Greek-origin name 'Myra' (from Greek myron 'fragrant oil'), adopted into Indian diaspora usage. No MW lemma. Parents associate with 'beloved' or 'admired'.

name: Naina
etymology: Hindi/Punjabi word from naina (eyes), from Sanskrit nayana. The personal-name usage is modern North Indian colloquial.

name: Nakul
etymology: Son of Mādrī by the younger Aśvin; fourth of the five Pāṇḍava brothers; expert horseman.

name: Naman
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. namana (bending, bowing)

name: Nandini
etymology: Daughter; a cow; daughter of Surabhi-Kāmadhenu — the divine cow protected by King Dilīpa in Raghuvaṃśa Sarga 2.

name: Nandita
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. nandita (gladdened, pleased, happy)

name: Narayan
etymology: The eternal Spirit pervading the universe; Viṣṇu in his cosmic-form aspect; the primeval son of (the primeval) Man.

name: Narendra
etymology: King; prince; lord of men; also a physician/master of antidotes in Daśakumāracarita.

name: Navya
etymology: Praiseworthy, to be praised; new, fresh — synonym of navīna per Apte.

name: Neel
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. nīla (dark-blue, indigo)

name: Neelam
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. nīla / nīla-maṇi (a sapphire)

name: Neeta
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. nīta (led, well-behaved, modest)

name: Neha
etymology: Hindi/Bengali word from sneha (affection, MW) — the dropped 's' form Nehā as personal name is 20th-century colloquial.

name: Nidhi
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. nidhi (a store, hoard, treasure)

name: Nikhil
etymology: MW ni-khila:

name: Nirav
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. nīrava (noiseless, still)

name: Nirvi
etymology: Modern Sanskritic-flavored coinage. Components draw on nir- prefix but compound as feminine name is 21st-century.

name: Nischay
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. niścaya (conviction, certainty, resolve)

name: Nitya
etymology: Eternal, constant, perpetual; epithet of Durgā/Lalitā; the 16 Nityās of Śrīvidyā Tantric tradition.

name: Nivaan
etymology: Modern Sanskritic-flavored coinage in 2010s-2020s urban India. No MW lemma; sometimes marketed as derived from nivāsa but that link is unverified.

name: Nivedita
etymology: MW (ppp.):

name: Nyra
etymology: shining

name: Ojas
etymology: Bodily strength, vigour, energy, ability, power; vitality (the principle of vital warmth and action throughout the body).

name: Om
etymology: The mystical syllable composed of a-u-m representing Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva — the praṇava.

name: Padma
etymology: Name of Śrī-Lakṣmī ('the lotus-one'); the auspicious goddess of fortune; consort of Viṣṇu.

name: Palash
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. palāśa (a leaf, foliage; Butea frondosa tree)

name: Pallavi
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. pallava (a sprout, shoot, twig, spray)

name: Pari
etymology: Pari — Persian loanword 'fairy'; widely adopted in Hindi/Urdu and Indian English. No MW Sanskrit lemma. Popular 2010+ urban Indian naming.

name: Parth
etymology: Metronymic of the Pāṇḍavas — especially Arjuna son of Kuntī (Pṛthā); used pervasively in the Bhagavad Gītā vocative.

name: Parthiv
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. pārthiva (earthly, relating to earth; a king, prince)

name: Parv
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. parvan (a knot, joint; a festival, sacred season)

name: Parvati
meaning: Daughter of the mountain; Śiva's consort
etymology: Daughter of Himavat king of the snowy mountains; consort of Śiva; central goddess of Kumārasambhava and the Śaiva tradition.

name: Pavani
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. pāvana (purifying, holy; fem. pāvanī, the Ganges)

name: Phalgun
meaning: Born under Uttara-Phālgunī; the lunar month
etymology: Epithet of Arjuna born under Uttara-Phālgunī asterism; lunar month Phālguna (Feb-Mar).

name: Pihu
etymology: Hindi onomatopoeia for the peacock's call; used as feminine endearment-name in 2010s urban families. No Sanskrit lemma.

name: Pitambara
etymology: MW: 'dressed in yellow clothes; N. of Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa.' Yellow robe was worn by Budha at birth; symbolises the metres of the Vedas.

name: Piyush
etymology: Pīyūṣa — the food of the gods, ambrosia, nectar; the immortality-drink produced at the churning of the milk-ocean. Attested from Ṛgveda onwards.

name: Piyusha
etymology: Feminine of Pīyūṣa. PW attests fem. nominative 'pīyūṣā'. Same semantic range: nectar, ambrosia, divine drink.

name: Pooja
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. pūjā (honour, worship, respect, reverence)

name: Poonam
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. pūrṇimā (day of full moon); 'Poonam' modern Hindi form

name: Pragya
etymology: Discrimination, judgement, intelligence, wisdom; in Buddhism, transcendental wisdom; personified as Sarasvatī.

name: Prakash
etymology: Brightness, light, lustre; manifestation, expansion, diffusion; in Kashmir Śaivism the light of consciousness identified with Śiva.

name: Pranav
etymology: The mystical or sacred syllable oṃ; the quintessence of the Vedas; an epithet of Viṣṇu / the Supreme Being.

name: Pransh
etymology: Modern -ansh family coinage. Components MW but compound as personal name is 21st-century.

name: Prerna
etymology: Impulse, instigation, incitement; in modern usage, inspiration, motivation.

name: Prisha
etymology: Modern Sanskritic-flavored coinage marketed as 'loved by god'; no MW lemma. Popular post-2010 in urban India.

name: Priya
etymology: MW priya:

name: Priyanka
etymology: MW priyaṃ-kara mf(ī or ā)n.:

name: Punya
etymology: Auspicious, propitious, pure, holy; virtue, religious merit.

name: Pushkal
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. puṣkala (rich, full, abundant, excellent)

name: Pushpa
etymology: Feminine of puṣpa; a common feminine name.

name: Radha
etymology: Prosperity, success; Kṛṣṇa's dearest consort; one of the two forms of Lakṣmīdevī.

name: Rahul
etymology: Buddha's son; meaning 'capable,' 'efficient,' or 'conqueror of all miseries.'

name: Raj
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. rājan (a king, sovereign); rāj to reign, rule

name: Rajat
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. rajata (silver; of silver colour)

name: Rajesh
etymology: Compositional rāja + īśa

name: Ram
etymology: The pleasing one; the seventh avatāra of Viṣṇu in the tretāyuga; hero of the Rāmāyaṇa; prince of Ayodhyā.

name: Rama
etymology: The charming one; an epithet of Lakṣmī; the delightful one.

name: Ramesh
etymology: MW rameśa (Kāvya, Purāṇa) = ramādhipa:

name: Rani
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. rājñī (a queen, wife of a king); 'Rani' modern Hindi form

name: Rekha
etymology: A line, streak, mark; range, row; sketch; line on the palm (destiny); pervasive in kāvya.

name: Reyansh
etymology: Modern Indian masculine coinage; no Monier-Williams lemma. Folk etymology: 'rey' (ray of light) + 'aṃśa' (portion/part). Popular 2018–2025 urban Indian naming.

name: Rishabh
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ṛṣabha 'a bull; the best or most excellent of its kind'

name: Riya
etymology: Modern feminine hypocoristic; sometimes marketed as from Riyā (a river in Latvia) or Sanskrit but no clear etymology. Popular 2000s-onward.

name: Rohan
etymology: Rising, mounting; act of ascending, growth, increase; also name of a mountain in Laṅkā famous for gems.

name: Rohit
etymology: Adjective rohita 'red, ruddy' used as a proper name; epithet associated with the sun and with Agni.

name: Rohita
etymology: Son of King Hariścandra whose story is told in Aitareya-brāhmaṇa 7.13-18; also a form of Agni and a name of the sun.

name: Rudra
etymology: Vedic storm-god, prototype of Śiva; over 75 hymns address Rudra (RV 1.114, 2.33, 7.46).

name: Saanvi
etymology: Modern Indian feminine coinage; some sources gloss as 'one with the Lord' (sa + Anvī, an epithet of Lakṣmī). No Monier-Williams lemma. Popular 2010–2025 urban Indian naming.

name: Sachin
etymology: Modern Hindi/Marathi name, NOT an MW headword. Two circulating accounts, both citable, neither proven: (a) from Śacīndra (śacī + indra,

name: Sakshi
etymology: Witness; in Vedānta the pure awareness that witnesses all things.

name: Sanjay
etymology: Charioteer-minister to Dhṛtarāṣṭra; the narrator of the Bhagavad-gītā.

name: Shivansh
etymology: A modern Sanskritic compound: śiva + aṃśa

name: Shreya
etymology: MW śreyas:

name: Shyam
etymology: Dark color, swarthy, dark-blue; Kṛṣṇa epithet.

name: Shyama
etymology: Dark/black; mother of Tīrthaṅkara Vimala; goddess in vārāhyabhyudaya-maṇḍala.

name: Siddharth
etymology: One who has accomplished his aim or object; successful, prosperous; birth name of Gautama Buddha.

name: Siddhartha
meaning: She who has accomplished her aim
etymology: Feminine of Siddhārtha; in Jain tradition, name of the mother of the 4th Tīrthaṅkara Abhinandananātha.

name: Sita
meaning: Furrow; Janaka's daughter, wife of Rāma
etymology: 'The furrow' — King Janaka discovered Sītā in the furrow while consecrating the sacrificial field. Wife of Rāma, paragon of pativratā dharma, incarnation of Lakṣmī.

name: Siya
etymology: Modern short form of Sītā (MW-attested as Rāmāyaṇa heroine). Standalone Siyā as personal name is 20th-21st-century.

name: Sunil
etymology: MW su-nīla:

name: Suraj
etymology: Hindi tadbhava: sūraj

name: Suresh
etymology: MW sureśa:

name: Tanvi
etymology: Tanvī = slender-bodied, graceful woman; classical kāvya epithet. Sometimes used as epithet of Pārvatī.

name: Tara
etymology: MW:

name: Uma
etymology: Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat and consort of Śiva; also light, splendour; fame; tranquility; flax; turmeric.

name: Umesh
etymology: Apte s.v. umeśa (उमेश) 'lord of Umā, an epithet of Śiva'

name: Urmila
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. ūrmilā (ऊर्मिला) 'N. of a daughter of Janaka, wife of Lakṣmaṇa'

name: Usha
etymology: Dawn, morning, morning light; personified as daughter of heaven and sister of the Ādityas; one of the most-invoked Vedic goddesses.

name: Varun
etymology: One of oldest Vedic deities; chief of the Ādityas; lord of waters; guardian of ṛta; wielder of pāśa.

name: Ved
etymology: Veda — 'knowledge, true or sacred knowledge'; one of the four foundational Vedas (Ṛk, Sāma, Yajus, Atharva). MW: 'knowledge, true or sacred knowledge or lore, knowledge of ritual.' Foundational Sanskrit term.

name: Vedant
meaning: End of the Vedas; Vedanta philosophy
etymology: MW lemma vedānta exists for the philosophical school. Personal-name usage is modern 20th-century.

name: Veena
etymology: The Indian lute; held by Sarasvatī and Nārada; classical kāvya pervasive.

name: Vidhi
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. vidhi (विधि) 'rule, ordinance, fate; the Creator (Brahmā)'

name: Vidya
etymology: Knowledge, science, learning, scholarship; epithet of Sarasvatī; in Tantra one of the ten Mahāvidyās.

name: Vihaan
etymology: Morning, dawn (lexicographer-attested); modern spelling Vihaan widely used.

name: Vijay
etymology: Victory in all directions; epithet of Arjuna in Mbh; also a Viṣṇu epithet; one of Vaikuṇṭha's two gatekeepers (with Jaya).

name: Vikas
etymology: MW vi-kāsa:

name: Vishal
etymology: Monier-Williams s.v. viśāla (विशाल) 'large, spacious, great'

name: Vivaan
etymology: Vivān — present-active participle 'shining forth, life-giving'. MW: from vi-√an 'to breathe, live.' Some sources also Vedic 'wide-spreading'. Popular modern coinage with classical roots.

name: Yuvan
etymology: MW:
